question_text: An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension, ischemic heart disease and COPD, who underwent a complete rectocolonoscopy due to rectal bleeding, with the following findings: polypoid lesion 3 cm in diameter located 10 cm from the anal margin, occupying the half of the circumference. Rest of exploration without findings until blind. In the polyp biopsy, an adenocarcinoma limited to the submucosa is seen. Endorectal ultrasound: uT1N0. Pelvic MRI: T1N0. TC: No evidence of disease at a distance. What will be the most likely therapeutic decision to be made in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission?

        ### Question
        An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension, ischemic heart disease and COPD, who underwent a complete rectocolonoscopy due to rectal bleeding, with the following findings: polypoid lesion 3 cm in diameter located 10 cm from the anal margin, occupying the half of the circumference. Rest of exploration without findings until blind. In the polyp biopsy, an adenocarcinoma limited to the submucosa is seen. Endorectal ultrasound: uT1N0. Pelvic MRI: T1N0. TC: No evidence of disease at a distance. What will be the most likely therapeutic decision to be made in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission?

        ### Options
        opa. Abdominal-perineal rectum amputation.
opb. Neoadjuvant radiotherapy and low anterior resection of the rectum by laparoscopy.
opc. Transanal endoscopic microsurgery.
opd. Anterior low resection of laparotomic rectus.
ope. Anterior low resection of laparoscopic rectal route and adjuvant radiotherapy.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Polypoid lesion identified -> Biopsy reveals adenocarcinoma limited to submucosa -> Staging indicates uT1N0 -> No evidence of distant disease -> Surgical resection is indicated -> Low anterior resection is appropriate for T1N0 -> Confidence in low anterior resection as a treatment option is high -> 85%
CHAIN: Polypoid lesion found during colonoscopy -> Biopsy shows submucosal adenocarcinoma -> Staging confirms uT1N0 -> No metastasis detected on imaging -> Multidisciplinary team considers surgical options -> Neoadjuvant therapy not necessary for T1N0 -> Low anterior resection is a standard approach -> Confidence in low anterior resection is moderate -> 80%
CHAIN: Rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed -> Limited to submucosa (uT1N0) -> No lymph node involvement -> Surgical intervention is required -> Transanal endoscopic microsurgery is less invasive -> May not achieve adequate margins for T1N0 -> Low anterior resection preferred for complete resection -> Confidence in low anterior resection is high -> 90%
CHAIN: Rectal cancer identified -> Staging shows uT1N0 -> No distant metastasis -> Surgical options evaluated by tumor board -> Abdominal-perineal resection is more invasive -> Low anterior resection is less invasive and effective -> Confidence in low anterior resection as a treatment option is high -> 85%

           - Remove/adjust steps contradicting known facts.
           - If paths confirm or clarify a point aligned with consensus, use them.
           - Ignore irrelevant or overly broad paths that don't help.
        3. If uncertain, note uncertainty but choose the best consensus-supported interpretation.
